evidence.claim: The Government of Ethiopia declared an immediate indefinite humanitarian truce to expedite aid into Tigray and said it hoped to reduce suffering and avoid further bloodshed.
evidence.title: Gov't Declares Indefinite Humanitarian Truce - ENA English - ENA
evidence.excerpt: The Government of Ethiopia declared an immediate indefinite humanitarian truce to expedite aid into Tigray and said it hoped to reduce suffering and avoid further bloodshed.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government announcement with a precise date and policy action; useful for ruler-attributed de-escalation, though self-serving.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and the opening de-escalation move of the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is government action under Abiy’s premiership; it shows executive choice, not just country context.
contrary_evidence: The truce did not end the conflict and later broke down.
Official framing may overstate humanitarian intent relative to battlefield realities.

evidence.claim: The Secretary-General welcomed Ethiopia’s indefinite humanitarian truce and urged all parties to turn it into a long-term ceasefire with restored public services and humanitarian access.
evidence.title: Welcoming Ethiopian Government’s Declaration of Indefinite Humanitarian Truce, Secretary-General Urges All Parties to Take Steps towards Lasting Ceasefire
evidence.excerpt: The Secretary-General welcomed Ethiopia’s indefinite humanitarian truce and urged all parties to turn it into a long-term ceasefire with restored public services and humanitarian access.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN statement corroborating the significance of the truce and its intended peace function.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and closely tied to the March ceasefire.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is to the Ethiopian government led by Abiy; the UN statement itself does not assign personal blame or credit beyond the state action.
contrary_evidence: The UN statement is supportive and not a forensic assessment of compliance.
It does not settle whether the government’s later conduct matched the truce.

evidence.claim: Negotiators for the Ethiopian government and Tigrayan forces were due to meet in Pretoria for the first formal peace talks since war began, after government and allied forces including Eritrean troops captured several towns.
evidence.title: First peace talks on Ethiopia's Tigray conflict to start in South Africa
evidence.excerpt: Negotiators for the Ethiopian government and Tigrayan forces were due to meet in Pretoria for the first formal peace talks since war began, after government and allied forces including Eritrean troops captured several towns.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting gives a useful contemporaneous bridge between battlefield pressure and the opening of talks.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and immediately before formal negotiations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is relevant to Abiy’s record because it links government-led military pressure and diplomacy in the same period, while also showing external Eritrean involvement in the theater.
contrary_evidence: The article does not establish Abiy’s personal direction over Eritrean troop movements.
The UCDP structured prior classifies the year as state-based conflict rather than internationalized conflict, so the cross-border element is narratively reported rather than structurally dominant.

evidence.claim: The ceasefire text required both sides to end hostilities, including air strikes, sabotage, hostile propaganda, rhetoric, and hate speech, and to move toward disarmament and restoration of constitutional order.
evidence.title: Factbox-Key points in Ethiopia's ceasefire agreement
evidence.excerpt: The ceasefire text required both sides to end hostilities, including air strikes, sabotage, hostile propaganda, rhetoric, and hate speech, and to move toward disarmament and restoration of constitutional order.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters summary of the published agreement text is a strong source for the concrete settlement terms.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and immediately after the Pretoria agreement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The terms are attributable to the government and Tigrayan side together, with Abiy’s government party represented in the deal.
contrary_evidence: A factbox on text terms does not prove implementation quality.
It leaves open whether hostile propaganda and force actually stopped on the ground.

evidence.claim: The UN commission said there were reasonable grounds to believe the federal government committed crimes against humanity in Tigray and that violations and abuses continued with impunity.
evidence.title: International Commission of Human Rights Experts on Ethiopia
evidence.excerpt: The UN commission said there were reasonable grounds to believe the federal government committed crimes against humanity in Tigray and that violations and abuses continued with impunity.
evidence.source_locator: Story text summarizing the Human Rights Council briefing
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN newsroom summary of an official commission briefing is strong evidence for civilian-harm and accountability findings.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and highly relevant to the conflict record before the November agreement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is to federal government forces and allied actors, which matters for Abiy because he was the head of government; the report does not isolate every battlefield order by him personally.
contrary_evidence: This is not a criminal judgment and does not assign every incident to Abiy personally.
It is an atrocity assessment, not a peace-process success metric.

evidence.claim: HRW said the government maintained an effective siege on Tigray through 2022 and that from late August to November 16 no humanitarian convoys entered the region.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Ethiopia
evidence.excerpt: HRW said the government maintained an effective siege on Tigray through 2022 and that from late August to November 16 no humanitarian convoys entered the region.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual rights report synthesizing 2022 conditions with concrete access chronology and accountability concerns.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but explicitly about 2022 conduct and conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is relevant to Abiy because the siege and access restrictions were government-side choices during his premiership.
contrary_evidence: It is retrospective and synthesizes many events rather than a single contemporaneous decision.
The report also notes abuses by Tigrayan forces and broader regional conflict dynamics.

evidence.claim: The UN said a WFP convoy reached Mai Tsebri in Tigray for the first time since June 2021, describing it as the first convoy movement since the peace agreement and noting resumed flight access.
evidence.title: Noon briefing of 16 November 2022
evidence.excerpt: The UN said a WFP convoy reached Mai Tsebri in Tigray for the first time since June 2021, describing it as the first convoy movement since the peace agreement and noting resumed flight access.
evidence.source_locator: Ethiopia section of the noon briefing
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN operational update on implementation of the November agreement and humanitarian access.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the immediate post-agreement period in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects implementation under the federal government’s peace posture, though operational access also depended on other parties and local conditions.
contrary_evidence: A single convoy does not prove broad compliance or durable peace.
The update describes progress, not a full normalization of the situation.

evidence.claim: The advisory note welcomed the November 2 peace agreement and said Article 10(3) required a comprehensive transitional justice policy aimed at accountability, truth, redress, reconciliation, and healing.
evidence.title: OHCHR-EHRC joint advisory note on Transitional Justice
evidence.excerpt: The advisory note welcomed the November 2 peace agreement and said Article 10(3) required a comprehensive transitional justice policy aimed at accountability, truth, redress, reconciliation, and healing.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Joint UN/EHRC advisory note with a direct reading of the peace-agreement accountability clause.
evidence.period_fit: Late 2022 and directly tied to the peace agreement’s implementation architecture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is government-linked commitment under Abiy’s premiership, but it is still a policy promise rather than proof of full implementation.
contrary_evidence: Consultations in Tigray were postponed because fighting resumed in August.
A transitional-justice promise is not the same as completed accountability.
